subject: Observability add-ons — packaging, usage credits, and exit clause options
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
To: Kendra Morris <kendra.morris@stellara.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Observability add-ons — packaging, usage credits, and exit clause options

Hi Kendra —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation I pulled together three packaging options for Stellara that combine retention, tracing, and advanced dashboards. The intent is to give you predictable unit costs while leaving flexible off-ramps in case usage patterns differ during Q1.

High-level options attached (SOW + pricing workbook). Short summary below and a couple of specific questions for your procurement team so we can finalize a draft SOW: 

- Option A — Pilot: 6-month, slab pricing for retention + tracing with a small dashboard seat license. Includes 1 full export/month and up to 20M trace events/month.
- Option B — Standard: 12-month slab commitment with 20% lower per-unit than Pilot, tiered overage policy, and a single demo credit.
- Option C — Committed: 12-month committed spend with deeper discounts, reserved trace throughput (for consistent latency), and 60-day exit clause tied to a defined usage threshold (see term sheet).

Questions for procurement:
1) Would Stellara accept a usage-based true-up on a monthly cadence (vs. quarterly)?
2) For the exit clause in Option C, do you need a fixed financial cap or an operational trigger (e.g., <40% utilization over 2 months)?

If useful, Ben can propose a concession path (credits + staged discounts) we can show to finance/legal. Marcus will validate throughput SLAs for committed capacity.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call with your team this week.

—
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aisha.rahman@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOW_v2_Stellara.pdf (application/pdf), pricing_workbook_stellara.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Kendra Morris <kendra.morris@stellara.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 13 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Observability add-ons — packaging, usage credits, and exit clause options

Aisha —

Appreciate the options and the clean workbook. A few quick items from our side after a sync with James & procurement: 

- Monthly true-ups are preferred (helps match our internal chargeback cadence).
- For Option C the legal and finance teams will not accept an open-ended 60-day exit without a financial cap. If you can propose a cap formula (e.g., 2x monthly committed spend as the maximum severance) that would be a good starting point.
- We want an explicit definition of "trace event" and the retention window assumptions (e.g., does retention include hot + cold storage or just hot?).

Can you confirm whether the demo credit in Option B can be converted to additional retention credits if unused? That would make Option B more attractive.

Also copying procurement for timing — procurement, do you need a redline of the term sheet or is a condensed commercial summary sufficient to start internal approvals?

Thanks,
Kendra

Kendra Morris
Director, Observability Platform
Stellara Systems
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Kendra Morris <kendra.morris@stellara.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Observability add-ons — packaging, usage credits, and exit clause options

Kendra —

Thanks for the quick read. A couple proposed fixes that should make procurement & finance comfortable: 

- Exit cap: propose a fixed severance equal to 2.5x the committed monthly payment for the remainder of the term, capped at the value of three monthly payments. For example, if committed monthly is $40k, max exit payment would be $120k.
- Trace event definition: we'll add a glossary line in the SOW: "trace event = a single span ingress that is indexed for search; aggregated logs and metrics are not counted as trace events." Retention includes both hot and cold tiers; hot retention is counted against quota, cold is included but at a lower effective cost after archival.
- Demo credit in Option B: yes — we can make it convertible to retention credits at a 1:1 discount rate up to a cap of $15k.

I've attached a one-page commercial summary and a version of the term sheet that reflects the cap. Marcus: can you confirm SLA adjustments if we reserve trace throughput for Stellara under Option C?

Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-obs-term-sheet.pdf (pdf)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 15 Dec 2026 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Observability add-ons — packaging, usage credits, and exit clause options

All —

I validated the Option C reserved throughput numbers with infra: reserving the requested baseline 700 tps of trace ingestion for the committed plan requires 2x the burst buffer configuration we normally provision. We can provide a 99.9% ingest latency SLA at that reservation level, and we'll include a usage report feed to Stellara's S3 bucket for transparency.

Two operational notes to surface for the SOW: 
1) If utilization drops below the operational trigger (40% of reserved for two consecutive months) and an exit payment is triggered, we will also release reserved nodes within 30 days; there may be a short warm-up penalty if re-activation is requested within 90 days.
2) For the monthly true-up, we need the billing contact and an estimated initial monthly token/trace volume window so we can seed the first invoice accurately.

Marcus Lin
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Kendra / James / procurement team —

Quick note from legal to expedite redline: we're comfortable with the proposed exit cap formula Ben suggested provided we add a short clause that limits severance exposure if Stellara engages in gross misuse (defined list) or knowingly exceeds agreed-upon ingestion thresholds repeatedly. We'll prepare a condensed commercial summary and a draft redline of the SOW this afternoon.

Next steps (proposed):
- Redwood to send condensed commercial summary + redlined SOW by EOD today (attached).
- Stellara to confirm preferred billing contact and whether monthly or quarterly invoices are required by procurement (you previously said monthly preferred; please confirm).
- If procurement wants a 30-min alignment call, we can do Wednesday morning PST.

Kimberly Park
